product_backlog.description: Core functionality enabling users to manage lists and tasks.
product_backlog.title: Core To-Do List Management

product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.title: Create To-Do List
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Allows users to organize tasks into separate topical lists.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the main page, When they enter a list name and submit, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified that US-0001 acceptance criteria are met: creating a list via form works and displays correctly.

product_backlog.title: Add Task to List
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing to-do list, When the user enters a task description and clicks add, Then the task is added to that list.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Enables users to break down their lists into actionable tasks.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified that US-0002 acceptance criteria are met: adding tasks to an existing list works correctly and displays them under the list.

product_backlog.title: Ensure requirements.txt dependencies are included from the start of story implementation to avoid test collection errors during QA testing.
product_backlog.overview: Ensure requirements.txt dependencies are included from the start of story implementation to avoid test collection errors during QA testing.
acceptance_criteria: Given new dependencies are needed, When code is written, Then requirements.txt is updated immediately from the start of story implementation.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified that requirements.txt dependencies are properly included from the start of story implementation.

product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task in a list, When the user clicks the complete/incomplete toggle, Then the task status updates accordingly and is visually distinguished.
product_backlog.title: Mark Task Complete or Incomplete
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Provides feedback on task completion status.

acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user clicks the delete button for that task, Then the task is removed from the list.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove unwanted or obsolete items.
product_backlog.title: Delete Task
Delete Entire List
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can remove whole project categories when no longer needed.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing to-do list with or without tasks, When the user clicks the delete list button, Then the entire list and its associated tasks are removed.
Given multiple lists and tasks exist, When the user views the main dashboard, Then all lists are displayed and clicking a list shows all its tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished.
product_backlog.title: View All Lists and Tasks
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to see all my lists and their tasks with completed items visually distinguished so that I can review my overall progress.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Provides overview and navigation for all stored tasks.

sprint_backlog.overview: Ensure requirements.txt dependencies are included from the start of story implementation to avoid test collection errors during QA testing.
acceptance_criteria: Given new dependencies are needed, When code is written, Then requirements.txt is updated immediately from the start of story implementation.
sprint_backlog.approach: Ensure requirements.txt has all necessary dependencies upfront.
sprint_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified that requirements.txt dependencies are properly included from the start of story implementation.

messages.content: [SPRINT PHASE: Development] This sprint's Sprint Backlog is published - implement/review/test/accept its stories. Committing an additional Ready story into this sprint (plan_sprint_backlog_item) is fine here too if there's budget left; drafting brand-new backlog content (upsert_story/upsert_epic/etc.) still belongs in Conceptual Work/Plan & Start Sprint, not here.

This is sprint 2 of 5. Continue the product vision from before - check the existing repo content (specs/, code, .hc/state.json) before planning, so you build on what's already there rather than repeating or contradicting it. As before: the sprint goal and backlog are pre-approved. Start by calling start_sprint(goal) to officially kick off this sprint - it mechanically resets the sprint's own token/event budget, so skipping it leaves this sprint silently running on whatever budget the previous sprint already spent. Then proceed directly through planning, development, PR creation, CI verification, sprint review (create_sprint_report), and the release PR (create_release_pr) without waiting for further approval. Do not ask me anything else during this sprint.
